candidateClaims.title: Community attribution for weaving
candidateClaims.statement: The earlier research summary links nito weaving with Iraya-Mangyan artisans in Talipanan. Current practitioner accounts, the transmission of skills, and permission to reproduce particular designs have not been independently checked in this update.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Inherited research summary; current details unverified
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Read the cited program reports and obtain named-community review before adding maker biographies, demonstrations, or distinctive patterns.

candidateClaims.title: Competing name-change explanations
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier research notes flag a three-Theodores explanation of the town’s name as uncertain. This app does not establish that explanation as the origin of the name or identify a confirmed founder from it.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Locate the original account, compare local oral-history versions, and distinguish naming stories from administrative records.

candidateClaims.title: Community names need precise attribution
candidateClaims.statement: The earlier research summary names Iraya and Alangan communities in accounts of Baco. Community presence does not establish that every practice or design belongs to both communities; the relevant passages and present-day attribution still need review.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Check the historical passages and community-led sources separately; do not substitute Hanunó’o motifs for Iraya or Alangan material.

candidateClaims.title: Capital-transfer chronology remains unresolved
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier editorial notes report conflicting capital-transfer dates. No specific transfer date is added here as established history; cityhood and a change in administrative capital must not be treated as the same event.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Compare original administrative instruments and dated archival records before adopting a transfer chronology.

candidateClaims.title: Objects are not proof of a community’s identity
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier research notes caution against concluding that inhabitants were Chinese merely from a claim about imported pottery. The underlying archaeological evidence has not been checked here, and no ethnic identity or earliest-settlement date is established by this note.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Find excavation context, dating evidence, and specialist interpretation. Distinguish trade in objects from conclusions about the identity of residents.

candidateClaims.title: A descriptive label is not an exclusive designation
candidateClaims.statement: The earlier research summary describes Victoria as a fruit basket. The wording is not treated here as a formal, exclusive, or current statistical designation, and it does not establish that every pictured fruit is a major local crop.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Read the agricultural studies, retain their dates, and ask growers about the varieties and activities represented.

candidateClaims.title: 1962 and 1963: compare the records
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier research notes identify a conflict: one provincial summary gives 1962, while the cited Republic Act 3609 and LGU account identify 1963. This is presented as a source-comparison lead; the original legal text has not been retrieved again in this update.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Inherited conflicting dates; primary citation awaits rechecking
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Read the Act’s approval and effectivity provisions and compare them with the LGU chronology; do not choose a date by majority vote among websites.

candidateClaims.title: Recorded craft and current practice differ
candidateClaims.statement: The prior research records nipa weaving, but current practitioners, techniques, and the extent of present-day practice were not verified. A historical mention does not prove that every household practices the craft today.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Read the historical account and seek consent-based maker review before illustrating a specific technique or naming practitioners.

candidateClaims.title: Town-planning chronology needs corroboration
candidateClaims.statement: The earlier quick-facts summary links the town-seat transfer with 1916 and describes a planned center. These details still need comparison with dated planning records; the rainbow account remains a separate local legend.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Inherited planning summary; chronology not reverified
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Locate dated municipal planning or administrative records and keep the town-seat chronology separate from name-origin storytelling.

candidateClaims.title: Settlement accounts do not imply empty land
candidateClaims.statement: The earlier research summary connects Gloria’s development with Tambong and Maligaya and a former connection to Pinamalayan. The detailed settlement chronology has not been reverified; accounts of arriving migrants must not imply that the land had no earlier inhabitants.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Compare dated local histories with evidence about existing communities, land use, and migration before writing a founding narrative.

candidateClaims.title: Name meaning, language, and creation date
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier notes leave the specific language and community attribution of the basud name account unresolved. They also flag Republic Act 2514 as a lead to check before teaching a precise municipal creation date. Neither missing detail is supplied as a confirmed fact here.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Oral-account attribution and legal lead pending
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Locate the original legal instrument and a credible language or community source; do not infer a particular Mangyan language from a generic label.

candidateClaims.title: Political dates need source comparison
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier editorial notes identify disagreements between municipal and portal histories about some political dates. No disputed date is adopted here. Buhid and Bangon narratives also require separate contributor attribution rather than being blended into one community story.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Reported chronological conflict and attribution gaps
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Compare dated administrative records and named-community accounts before expanding the local political or cultural narrative.

candidateClaims.title: Paclasan and the palasan account
candidateClaims.statement: The inherited material connects Roxas with Paclasan and preserves a palasan-palm name account. This update has not established a sole origin, a confirmed first-settlement date, or the original language attribution of that explanation.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Inherited local name account; origin not established
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Compare the original history passages, older administrative records, and local accounts before presenting a single origin story.

candidateClaims.title: Association does not grant permission to reproduce
candidateClaims.statement: The inherited NCCA citation connects Ginaw Bilog, Mansalay, and ambahan. That association does not establish permission to reproduce particular verses, translations, recordings, or motifs; none of those materials is newly introduced through this note.
candidateClaims.evidenceLabel: Inherited institutional citation; reuse permissions unconfirmed
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Read the cited cultural account and arrange community-led review, attribution, and appropriate permissions before reproducing expressive material.

candidateClaims.title: Mait and early settlement: a hypothesis
candidateClaims.statement: Earlier research notes describe the identification of an old town with Mait as a hypothesis, not settled proof of a tenth-century settlement. This app does not present that identification or date as an established origin for Bulalacao.
candidateClaims.verificationNeeded: Locate the underlying historical and archaeological arguments, check dates and geographic identification, and compare scholarly alternatives before asserting continuity with a present-day municipality.
